en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
Methods for Settling Legal Issues (Adhikaraṇasamatha)
Venerable sirs, these seven principles for the settling of legal issues come up for recitation.
For the settling and pacification of legal issues as they arise,
the resolution face-to-face (sammukhāvinaya) should be granted.
A verdict of mindfulness should be granted;
a verdict of past insanity should be granted;
a formal act based on admission should be carried out.
The majority decision,
the further penalty for one who is worse,
and the covering over as with grass.
Venerable friends, the seven principles for settling legal issues have been recited.
In this regard, I ask the venerable ones:
"Are you pure in this matter?"
A second time I ask:
"Are you pure in this matter?
A third time I ask:
“Are you pure in this matter?
“The venerable ones are pure in this matter; therefore they are silent. Thus do I understand it.
The methods for settling legal issues are concluded.
Venerable sirs, the introduction has been recited;
the four rules entailing defeat have been recited;
the thirteen rules involving formal meeting of the Saṅgha have been recited.
The two undetermined rules have been recited;
the thirty rules on forfeiture and confession have been recited;
the ninety-two rules on confession have been recited.
The four rules on matters to be confessed have been recited;
the rules of training have been recited;
the seven principles for settling legal issues have been recited.
So much of what has come down in the discourses of that Blessed One, included within the discourses, comes up for recitation every half-month.
"In this matter, all should train together, in harmony, in mutual agreement, and without dispute.
The Mahāvibhaṅga is finished.
